title: Pembrolizumab every 3 weeks for head and neck cancer
context_label: First-line treatment of metastatic or unresectable recurrent head and neck squamous cell carcinoma with a tumour PD-L1 combined positive score (CPS) of at least 1. This indication excludes nasopharyngeal cancer and cancer progressing within six months after curatively intended systemic treatment for locoregionally advanced disease.
indication_text: First-line treatment of metastatic or unresectable recurrent head and neck squamous cell carcinoma with a tumour PD-L1 combined positive score (CPS) of at least 1. This indication excludes nasopharyngeal cancer and cancer progressing within six months after curatively intended systemic treatment for locoregionally advanced disease.
purpose: Pembrolizumab aims to control head and neck cancer that has returned or spread, relieve symptoms and help some people live longer. Benefit and side effects are reviewed for you.
schedule_summary: Pembrolizumab 200 mg is given through a vein over about 30 minutes on Day 1 every 3 weeks. The whole visit includes safety checks, preparation and observation. Treatment continues until progression or unacceptable toxicity. After 24 months of sustained response without progression, the team may consider stopping; stopping at 24 months is not automatic.
administration_text: Pembrolizumab 200 mg is given through a vein over about 30 minutes on Day 1 every 3 weeks. The whole visit includes safety checks, preparation and observation.
monitoring_summary: Full blood count, kidney and liver tests and glucose before every 3-week cycle. Thyroid tests every 3–6 weeks; cortisol when clinically indicated.

agents.name: Pembrolizumab
agents.explanation: Pembrolizumab is an antibody that blocks PD-1, a control switch on immune T cells. Cancer cells can use this switch to reduce immune attack. Blocking it can help the immune system recognise and attack cancer. The same increased immune activity can inflame healthy organs, which is why new symptoms need attention even after treatment ends.
agents.watch: Report new breathing, bowel, skin, hormone, heart or nerve symptoms promptly; these may be immune inflammation.
risks: Immune inflammation of lungs, bowel, liver, kidneys, hormone glands, skin, heart and nervous system
Some effects need steroids, hospital care or long-term hormone replacement
Effects may start after the final dose
Heart, muscle and nerve immune effects can occur together and require urgent assessment

monitoring_schedule.title: Required safety checks and your individual cancer-assessment plan

rows.label: Bloods and organ safety
cells: Full blood count, kidney and liver tests, glucose and thyroid tests; review autoimmune disease, transplants, previous immune side effects and all medicines. Confirm the tumour PD-L1 combined positive score; this is a tumour test, not a routine blood test.
Full blood count, kidney and liver tests and glucose before every 3-week cycle. Thyroid tests every 3–6 weeks; cortisol when clinically indicated.
New symptoms may require extra tests before the next planned review.
Safety bloods do not by themselves show whether treatment controls the cancer.

Keep reporting new symptoms after treatment ends. Steroid tapers, hormone replacement or specialist review may continue longer. Scans and examinations follow your individual response and follow-up plan.

rows.label: Thyroid and other hormones
cells: Baseline thyroid function and glucose.
Thyroid tests every 3–6 weeks, including between six-week visits when due.
Report marked thirst, unusual fatigue, dizziness, headache or weakness.
Cortisol or other hormone tests when clinically indicated.
Continue prescribed hormone replacement and monitoring when needed.

rows.label: Head and neck function
cells: Record weight, intake, swallowing, speech and existing mouth or dental problems.
Review pain, intake, weight and support needs.
Report choking, inability to drink, worsening swallowing or new neck symptoms.
Agree examinations and scans with the oncology team.
Continue rehabilitation and symptom support as needed.

rows.label: Medicines and practical plan
cells: Confirm the exact prescription, treatment aim and actual urgent contacts.
Bring your medicine list, current support plan and treatment record.
Record symptoms and medicines taken; ask before adding a new product.
Confirm any pause, dose change or stop in writing.
Record the final dose and the teams responsible for follow-up.

monitoring_schedule.note: These stages are not equal time intervals. Your team provides dates and reviews results. There is no universal blood tumour-marker panel or scan interval in this guide.

monitoring_test_details.label: Full blood count
monitoring_test_details.purpose: Checks blood cells and helps assess infection, anaemia and bleeding risk.
monitoring_test_details.timing: Before starting and before each treatment cycle

monitoring_test_details.label: Kidney and liver tests
monitoring_test_details.purpose: Checks for organ injury, including possible immune inflammation.
monitoring_test_details.timing: Before starting and before each cycle

monitoring_test_details.label: Blood glucose
monitoring_test_details.purpose: Checks blood sugar and possible treatment-related diabetes.

monitoring_test_details.label: Thyroid function
monitoring_test_details.purpose: Checks for an underactive or overactive thyroid.

monitoring_test_details.label: Cortisol
monitoring_test_details.purpose: Assesses possible adrenal or pituitary problems when symptoms or findings suggest them.

monitoring_test_details.label: Tumour PD-L1 combined positive score
monitoring_test_details.purpose: Checks whether the cancer meets this monotherapy indication; CPS is different from the lung tumour proportion score.

monitoring_test_details.label: Scans and head and neck examination
monitoring_test_details.purpose: Assesses the cancer and the response to treatment separately from safety bloods.
monitoring_test_details.timing: As prescribed in the individual disease-assessment plan

anatomy: Severe headache, confusion, weakness, dizziness or marked thirst need prompt advice.
New cough or breathlessness can signal inflammation or another urgent cause.
Chest pain, racing heartbeat or fainting needs urgent assessment.
Yellow eyes/skin or dark urine may signal inflammation; tests also check the liver.
Report much less urine, new swelling or a change in kidney tests.
New or persistent diarrhoea, blood in stools or severe tummy pain needs urgent advice.
Report a spreading rash, painful skin, blisters or peeling promptly.
Severe weakness, drooping eyelids, swallowing or breathing difficulty can be urgent immune effects.
New blurred vision, painful eyes or visual change needs prompt advice.

support.title: Immune alert card and treatment holds
support.text: Carry your immune alert card during and after pembrolizumab. Tell any clinician that you have received immunotherapy. Do not restart a held treatment or change prescribed steroids or hormone replacement yourself.

support.title: Eating and weight
support.text: Tell the team early if swallowing, appetite, pain or taste changes reduce intake. A dietitian can agree practical food, drink or feeding support with you. Do not wait for substantial weight loss.

support.title: Mouth and dental care
support.text: Agree a mouth-care plan and tell your dentist about previous or current cancer treatment. Arrange oncology advice before dental procedures, particularly after head and neck radiation.

support.title: Swallowing and communication
support.text: Ask for speech and language therapy if swallowing or speech is difficult. Use the food textures, exercises and communication support advised for you; a general guide cannot establish safe swallowing.

support.title: Medicines and fertility
support.text: Bring prescribed, over-the-counter and herbal medicines and supplements for review. Discuss fertility preservation and breastfeeding before treatment. Use effective contraception during treatment and for at least four months after the final dose. Tell the team promptly about a possible pregnancy. Do not breastfeed without specific advice from the team.

items.title: What treatment aims to do
items.text: Pembrolizumab aims to control head and neck cancer that has returned or spread, relieve symptoms and help some people live longer. Benefit and side effects are reviewed for you.

items.title: Choosing between treatments
items.text: Your team weighs the cancer, previous treatment, health, symptoms and preferences when discussing options. Other systemic treatment, local treatment where suitable, trials or symptom-focused care may be discussed.

chapters.title: How your treatment works
chapters.intro: Cancer treatment can also affect healthy tissue.

items.title: Pembrolizumab
items.text: Pembrolizumab is an antibody that blocks PD-1, a control switch on immune T cells. Cancer cells can use this switch to reduce immune attack. Blocking it can help the immune system recognise and attack cancer. The same increased immune activity can inflame healthy organs, which is why new symptoms need attention even after treatment ends.

chapters.title: Your treatment schedule
chapters.intro: Keep one calendar for treatment, tests and other appointments.

items.title: Receiving treatment
items.text: Pembrolizumab 200 mg is given through a vein over about 30 minutes on Day 1 every 3 weeks. The whole visit includes safety checks, preparation and observation.

items.title: Length of the course
items.text: Treatment continues until progression or unacceptable toxicity. After 24 months of sustained response without progression, the team may consider stopping; stopping at 24 months is not automatic.

items.title: A pause or change
items.text: Your team may pause or stop treatment to assess side effects. Record the reason, required tests and who can authorise restarting. A new cycle does not erase earlier severe toxicity.

chapters.title: Tests and review
chapters.intro: Blood safety tests, tumour tests and scans answer different questions.

items.text: Full blood count, kidney and liver tests, glucose and thyroid tests; review autoimmune disease, transplants, previous immune side effects and all medicines. Confirm the tumour PD-L1 combined positive score; this is a tumour test, not a routine blood test.

chapters.title: When and how to get help
chapters.intro: Use the oncology service’s written urgent-contact plan.

items.title: Contact the team promptly
items.text: Contact oncology immediately for new breathlessness, chest pain, diarrhoea, severe tummy pain, yellow skin or eyes, much less urine, severe headache, vision changes, marked weakness, confusion, unusual thirst or a spreading or blistering rash. Severe breathing difficulty, collapse or seizure is an emergency.

items.title: During an infusion or injection
items.text: Tell staff immediately about itching, a rash, dizziness, chest tightness, breathing difficulty, pain or swelling around the treatment site.

items.title: Prepare the handover
items.text: Tell the clinician the medicine name, date of the last dose, new symptoms and any prescribed steroids or hormone replacement. Carry the wallet card; do not delay urgent care while looking for a document.

chapters.title: Eating, mouth care and everyday support
chapters.intro: Ask for help before a practical problem prevents treatment.

items.title: Immune alert card and treatment holds
items.text: Carry your immune alert card during and after pembrolizumab. Tell any clinician that you have received immunotherapy. Do not restart a held treatment or change prescribed steroids or hormone replacement yourself.

items.title: Eating and weight
items.text: Tell the team early if swallowing, appetite, pain or taste changes reduce intake. A dietitian can agree practical food, drink or feeding support with you. Do not wait for substantial weight loss.

items.title: Mouth and dental care
items.text: Agree a mouth-care plan and tell your dentist about previous or current cancer treatment. Arrange oncology advice before dental procedures, particularly after head and neck radiation.

items.title: Swallowing and communication
items.text: Ask for individual speech and language therapy advice for swallowing or communication difficulties. Report choking, coughing with drinks or inability to swallow safely.

items.title: Energy and activity
items.text: Plan manageable activity and rest around symptoms. Tell the team about severe or unexpected fatigue, falls or difficulties managing at home.

chapters.title: Medicines, precautions and visit preparation
chapters.intro: Review medicines and practical needs before treatment.

items.title: Medicines and fertility
items.text: Bring prescribed, over-the-counter and herbal medicines and supplements for review. Discuss fertility preservation and breastfeeding before treatment. Use effective contraception during treatment and for at least four months after the final dose. Tell the team promptly about a possible pregnancy. Do not breastfeed without specific advice from the team.

items.title: Access and observation
items.text: Your team chooses suitable venous access for an infusion. A port, if used, has its own insertion, care and removal plan; it is not removed after each visit. No take-home chemotherapy pump is part of this regimen.

items.title: Work, transport and communication
items.text: Discuss transport, work, caring responsibilities, interpreter needs and a support person. Ask how results and changes will be communicated and who books your next tests.

chapters.title: Your record and contact card
chapters.intro: Keep the information that another clinician would need.

items.title: Cycle or review record
items.text: Record the cycle received, date, route, dose if supplied, important symptoms, any hold and the next agreed review. Stamp boxes record treatment received; they do not authorise the next dose.

items.title: Contacts and documents
items.text: Have the team replace example telephone numbers with your actual daytime and out-of-hours contacts. Carry the front/back wallet card and immune alert card when applicable. The printed handbook contains the key information without needing to scan a QR code.

items.title: Questions for review
items.text: Bring your main question, changes in swallowing or weight, symptoms, medicine changes and any concerns about the treatment aim. Ask for the plan in words you can explain back.

chapters.title: Evidence and further information
chapters.intro: Use evidence to support a personal treatment discussion.

items.title: What studies can tell us
items.text: KEYNOTE-048 supports pembrolizumab alone in the PD-L1-positive first-line recurrent or metastatic population. It compared treatment groups, not an individual prognosis. The trial used 200 mg every three weeks; the six-week schedule is not a separate randomised head and neck survival comparison.

items.title: Your individual decision
items.text: Group results cannot predict what will happen for you. Ask which benefits matter for your situation and how the team will decide whether treatment remains worthwhile.

items.title: Resources
items.text: The source list gives the official regimen and public patient information. Ask your team for a printed copy or help accessing a resource if needed.

evidence.title: Understanding the evidence
evidence.intro: Pembrolizumab aims to control head and neck cancer that has returned or spread, relieve symptoms and help some people live longer. Benefit and side effects are reviewed for you.
evidence.population: First-line treatment of metastatic or unresectable recurrent head and neck squamous cell carcinoma with a tumour PD-L1 combined positive score (CPS) of at least 1. This indication excludes nasopharyngeal cancer and cancer progressing within six months after curatively intended systemic treatment for locoregionally advanced disease.
evidence.comparison: Pembrolizumab alone versus cetuximab with platinum and fluorouracil in previously untreated recurrent/metastatic disease.
evidence.interpretation: KEYNOTE-048 supports pembrolizumab alone in the PD-L1-positive first-line recurrent or metastatic population. It compared treatment groups, not an individual prognosis. The trial used 200 mg every three weeks; the six-week schedule is not a separate randomised head and neck survival comparison.
limitations: Trial results describe groups; your individual benefit and risks may differ.
Do not transfer survival estimates between different cancer settings, schedules or treatment combinations.

consent_support: Discuss your diagnosis, intent, alternatives, expected benefit and uncertainty, treatment burden, serious or lasting harms, fertility and pregnancy precautions and your priorities. Include immune inflammation of lungs, bowel, liver, kidneys, skin, glands, heart, muscles, nerves and eyes; infusion or injection reactions; delayed effects; possible high-dose steroid treatment, permanent hormone replacement or permanent treatment stopping. Confirm actual urgent contacts and use teach-back. This draft does not authorise treatment.
